Streaming is a business decision wearing a technology costume. Event-to-action under one second changes fraud economics on instant rails.
Online/offline feature parity is what keeps serving honest.
Event-storming alignment decides whether you built a platform or a mess.
Where this goes wrong in practice
Where it breaks in practice: deferral: lineage and contracts scheduled for phase two, which arrives after the first regulator question does. By then every metric is a negotiation.

The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the spine-first thesis can become a two-year plumbing project nobody ships against. The spine is earned slice by slice, each one attached to a live decision.

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: underneath it sits the data spine: contracts, lineage and freshness SLAs that make the number trustworthy before anyone models it. Every program in the Data & Lakehouse domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Talk to the team that runs streaming is a business decision wearing a technology costume in production — the briefing is technical by design, and the first one costs nothing but the hour.
